title: Rigatoni alla norcina
subtitle: Short pasta with Italian sausage, cream, and black pepper
excerpt: Rigatoni alla norcina is an Umbrian pasta of Italian sausage, cream, and a generous amount of black pepper. The name comes from Norcia, the hill town famous for its pork butchery. It is a rich, quickly made dish: the sauce comes together in the time it takes to boil the pasta.
sourceNotes: Regional Umbrian recipe from the area around Norcia, historically known for its pork butchers and black truffles. Method drawn from Umbrian cooking traditions and Anna Del Conte, Gastronomy of Italy (2001).

glossaryTerms.definition: Italian culinary term meaning 'in the style of Norcia', an Umbrian town famous for pork products and black truffles; dishes alla norcina typically include pork sausage and sometimes truffle.

content.text: is the sausage-and-cream pasta of Umbria, where good pork is the foundation of the regional table. The sausagemeat is crumbled straight into the pan, crisped in its own fat, then finished with white wine and cream. A truffle paste or shaving is traditional; the dish is still excellent without it.

Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Crumble in {{sausage-meat}} of sausagemeat and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, for 6 to 8 minutes until golden and crisp in places. Transfer to a plate with a slotted spoon.

In the same pan, cook the shallots over medium heat for 3 minutes. Add {{garlic}} of garlic and cook for 1 minute more. Pour in {{dry-white-wine}} of wine, scraping up any bits from the bottom, and let it reduce by half.

Return the sausagemeat to the pan. Add {{double-cream}} of double cream and the truffle paste if using. Simmer for 3 minutes until the cream thickens slightly. Season well with black pepper and a little salt.

Cook {{pasta-dried}} of rigatoni in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water, then drain. Toss with the sauce, adding pasta water as needed. Stir in the Parmesan and serve immediately with extra pepper.

items.symptom: Sauce is too rich and heavy
items.cause: Cream proportion is high relative to the pasta water added.
items.fix: Thin with pasta water; the starch will bind the sauce and balance the cream.

items.symptom: Sausagemeat is grey rather than golden
items.cause: Pan was too crowded or heat was too low.
items.fix: Cook in two batches if the pan is not wide enough, or let it cook without stirring for 3 minutes before breaking it up.
A small amount of truffle paste or truffle oil (added off the heat) delivers a detectable note. Without it, the dish is a good sausage-cream pasta but not strictly norcina.

content.text: Norcia has been synonymous with fine pork butchery since at least the Middle Ages. The town's norcini (pork butchers) travelled across Italy and a norcino came to mean any skilled salami-maker. The pasta that bears the town's name celebrates that heritage: pork sausage, Umbrian black truffle if you can get it, good cream, and a great deal of pepper. In Norcia, the black truffle in season in December and January makes it a dish of real luxury.
